voiceover:
[conversational] One guy built a posting tool that now makes $50K a month.

[curious] And the move that made it work isn't the code. I'll tell you at the end.

It's called Post Bridge. You write one post, and it publishes to up to 10 platforms at once. It's for solo founders marketing their own business. Their pricing page says $39 a month for 15 accounts, unlimited posts.

[confident] These numbers are verified on TrustMRR. About $50K MRR. $45K in the last 30 days. 1,651 active subscriptions. 10% growth. [serious] Quick catch: that's revenue, not profit. We don't know what he keeps.

The founder is Jack Friks, a solo developer. He spent about four years struggling to make money online. Then he built the fix for his own posting headache in about a month.

[whispers] Here's the real lesson. He built in public on X and short-form video, and grew to 186.8K followers on X. Creators and solo marketers, exactly who buys a scheduler. He didn't hunt for customers. He was already standing in front of them.

[playful] Would you build this, or buy it?

Send this to the friend who keeps saying they'll launch something someday.

Hack saved?

topic: Business breakdown: POST BRIDGE — Post your content to multiple social media platforms at the same time, all-in one place.

pick.topic: Business breakdown: POST BRIDGE — Post your content to multiple social media platforms at the same time, all-in one place.
pick.angle: A solo founder built a 'post once, publish everywhere' tool that makes about $50K, and he grew it by posting on the same platforms it serves

research.what_it_does: A social media scheduler that publishes one post to up to 10 platforms at once (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Google Business). It also has an API and an MCP server for AI agents.
research.who_pays: Solo creators, founders and small teams who do their own marketing. The site says it is built for one person marketing a business.
research.pricing: Official pricing page: Marketer is $39/month for 15 connected accounts, billed monthly. Operator is $99/month for 99 accounts, then $1 per extra account with no maximum. Both plans have unlimited posts, a 7-day free trial and $0 due today. Per the About page, yearly billing saves two months. The pricing page lists API and MCP as included in Marketer. Operator adds team invites.
growth: Built to solve the founder's own problem. Per the Starter Story summary and a Stork.ai review, he made Post Bridge in late 2024 to cross-post for his first app, Curiosity Quench. It later grew '10 times, 100 times bigger' than that app (https://www.stork.ai/blog/his-selfish-app-replaced-hootsuite).

Founder X post: Curiosity Quench hit its first $15k month in September, and one month later he started Post Bridge to help scale it (https://x.com/jackfriks/status/1908506318165426344). On Apr 5, 2025 he posted that his 'little startup just hit 10k mrr'.

Build-in-public on X and short-form video. IndieMakerList says this has grown his X audience past 175,000 followers. Marketer Gems says Jack built an audience while building the product, and that this created natural distribution channels (https://www.marketergems.com/p/jack-friks-postbridge-story-personal-problem-to-profitable-saas).

Founder-led demos and education. In a July 2025 X post he explained a 'send as draft' TikTok feature and said he had seen 30+ million Instagram video views posting only through the API over 5 months (https://x.com/jackfriks/status/1947352793150324874).

Product-led SEO and positioning. The site has comparison pages such as 'Later alternatives', and its pricing pitch contrasts per-channel pricing with its own. Its About page says Buffer's $6 per channel makes 15 channels about $90/mo, versus $39/mo on Post Bridge.

AI-agent distribution. A Sept 11, 2026 GLOBE NEWSWIRE press release (a company-issued source) says Post Bridge was listed as a ChatGPT plugin, after an earlier listing in Anthropic's Claude connector directory. It reports 341, 508, 645 and 713 new signups on Sept 4–7, each an all-time daily record, against a previous average of about 50 a day (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/post-bridge-lands-inside-chatgpt-120000219.html).
Conversion work. A Side Hustler Story newsletter says he doubled the site's conversion rate from 2.2% to 4.32% with two changes (https://sidehustlerstory.substack.com/p/jack-friks).
founder_story: Jack Friks is a Canadian solo developer. The About page says Post Bridge is 'built by one person' and that he studied computer programming at Durham College. He still builds the product and answers support himself.

In his Indie Hackers post he says he spent about four years trying to make money online, including a year learning to code, and was still struggling to break $3k/mo. He says he cried on a walk three months before Post Bridge. He also says he built Post Bridge from scratch in about a month.

Before Post Bridge he built Curiosity Quench, an anti-doomscrolling mobile app. IndieMakerList and Stork.ai say it passed 100,000 downloads. He has since shipped other apps (Lovelee, Doof and others).
The company was founded in Sept 2024 and launched the following month. The legal entity is Jack Ingram Media Inc., Ontario, Canada (About page and press release).
lessons: Scratch your own itch. He spent about an hour a day posting the same content everywhere, so he built the tool he wanted. His first customer was himself, which is a ready-made use case for marketing.

Sell to the people you already reach. He markets his own apps with short-form content and posts about it publicly. His audience of creators and solo marketers is the same audience that buys the scheduler.
Be the cheap, simple option in a category full of bloated incumbents. Pricing is by accounts with unlimited posts, and the site compares itself directly against per-channel pricing from Buffer.
Ride new distribution surfaces early. The ChatGPT and Claude listings, plus MCP and API on every plan, produced record signups, according to the company press release.
Add features that answer real objections. The 'send as draft' TikTok feature came from users seeing zero views on API posts.
criticism: Revenue is not profit. TrustMRR shows the profit margin as masked (XX%), and no source gives the founder's profit or costs.

Churn may be high. A YouTube episode description (Tibo Maker, E12) claims 20% of customers leave every month. This is a third-party claim I could not trace to the founder's own data, so treat it as unconfirmed.

Competitive and commoditized market. Rivals include Buffer, Later, Hootsuite, Upload-Post (from $0) and Postiz (open source). Rival pages position it as a lean scheduler. Reviews say it has no inbox, no Canva integration and only beta analytics.

Platform dependency. The founder himself says API-based posting can get lower reach on TikTok and YouTube, and recommends manual posting for the first 10+ videos of a new account. The site says its own testing found no reach difference.

Heavy dependence on one founder's personal brand and a solo operation (186.8k X followers per TrustMRR). Third-party sources such as Indie Hackers describe an eight-month plateau before revenue doubled.
facts: TrustMRR (Stripe-verified): $49,969 MRR, $45,867 in the last 30 days, $570,991 all-time, 1,651 active subscriptions, and 10% growth vs the prior period.
Homepage counters (these change, so re-check before filming): 10 social platforms supported, 3,443,878 posts published by users, 2 min average time to post everywhere.
Indie Hackers, June 2026: Jack said it launched about 1.5 years earlier and makes $50k CAD ($35K USD) MRR. TrustMRR now shows about $50k MRR, so growth continued after that.
Press release (Sept 2026) says Post Bridge is bootstrapped with no outside funding and publishes its revenue in real time via TrustMRR.

Jack posted that he made $59,347 in May 2026 across his products (reported via an X trending summary). That figure covers his whole portfolio, not just Post Bridge, so don't use it as Post Bridge revenue.
Tech stack per TrustMRR: Next.js, Supabase, Stripe. In his Indie Hackers post he mentions using R2 to cut egress costs.
do_not_claim: Team size beyond 'solo founder'. The About page says one person, but check for contractors.
The $1M offer he reportedly declined in spring 2025. It appears only on jackfriks.com/wiki, an unverified secondary source, so I couldn't confirm it.
Pricing of '$29' or '$7.50/mo' or the older Starter/Creator/Pro plans. Those come from the press release and old review sites. The current pricing page shows $39 and $99, matching TrustMRR.
That ChatGPT or Claude listings caused the revenue growth. The press release reports only the signup spike and a count of 1,400+ paying customers. TrustMRR shows 1,651 active subscriptions.
Exact reach claims such as 'no reach difference'. These are the company's own claims.
research.notes: The reliable hook is the story of a solo founder who spent about four years failing, then built a tool for himself in about a month, and it reached about $50k MRR. Use TrustMRR for all current revenue numbers. Third-party review sites show old or wrong prices, so only use the official pricing page ($39 / $99). The pricing page snapshot I saw is labelled as old, but five third-party pages checked in Oct–Nov 2026 agree on $39 and $99, and TrustMRR matches. The homepage 'loved by 1,405 users' is older than TrustMRR's 1,651 active subscriptions, so don't show it. I verified the pricing page text only via search snippets, not a live visit. Re-check the exact wording on screen before recording. Some other facts above (e.g. 'Duration College', conversion-rate doubling) come from secondary sources. The press release is company-issued, not independent journalism.
